Posted to #83: https://github.com/jreinach-alt/hakuX/issues/83#issuecomment-5737707468

## Control verdict (the time-critical part): SOUND, but INERT

**Sound.** The folded BLEND_AND work cannot reach SRCCOPY, verified line by line against `55bc6c6c2b`:
- SRCCOPY branch is `blit.c:60-65`, unchanged since `24087af22a` (2026-01-15) — an ancestor of every ref in play.
- #38's whole diff is inside the `else if (... BLEND_AND)` arm; `blend_and_div()` is `static inline` under `__aarch64__`, called only from that loop.
- #84's leaf guard (`blit.c:140`) is inside that arm; its entry guard (`blit.c:499`) is conjoined with `operation == BLEND_AND`.
- The only shared edit is the `bytes_per_pixel` parameter. Inside `perform_blit()` its sole non-comment read is line 140. SRCCOPY never reads it.

**Inert, and that's the finding.** The eight captures' differing pixels aren't written by the blit at all, so the leg reads "unmoved" whatever the divide does. #83's `blocker_falsifier` is tautological — no world exists where it fires. **#38's PASS is unaffected** (its expect-values are live legs); only the sentence in `[issue.83] blocked_on` claiming the blocker is "now measured rather than argued" should be withdrawn.

Also corrected the brief: there is no #84 arm — #84 needs none, and the arm is #38's, already judged PASS on 2026-09-18.

## The mechanism: #83's premise is a column misread

The header is `... differing  max_rgb  max_a  pixels  off_by_one`. The row is `1650  1  0  307200  1650`. **"EXACTLY 1 px" is `max_rgb`** — the max channel delta. Five on-disk measurements read 1,573 / 1,650 / 1,650 / 1,701 / 1,701 pixels; none reads 1 as a count. The "1 px each" exists only in prose, propagated through the issue, the prediction JSON, `24a75d6e3c`'s commit message and an investigation doc.

The blit is **1×1** (`TestOverlapBarelyInclusive`), so one pixel is the ceiling on any copy-extent mechanism — the measurement is three orders of magnitude above it. The residual is vertex-colour interpolation in the Gouraud quad (`ELSEWHERE = 0`, all eight destination pixels byte-exact), and `dca3c94b98` — in arm A's ancestry, not in `b9d845d3`'s — is what took it from ~1,700 to 1. I flagged that this comparison confounds the commit with desktop-vs-device; it doesn't matter, since both candidates are outside `vk/blit.c`.

All three candidate shapes are refuted: `memmove` has no direction decision to get wrong, the only coordinate truncation needs a valid GPU tile pbkit doesn't set, and all ten `Clip_*`/`SRCCOPY_*` captures — the ones that actually exercise copy extents — score exactly 0.

## What reading can't settle

Which single pixel differs on a *device* capture at a ref carrying `dca3c94b98`. All the "which pixels" evidence is desktop. `docs/testing/blit_residual_anatomy.py <captures> <goldens>` decides it — no device, no arm, no build, re-reading captures that already exist.

**One thing I couldn't do:** I'm sandboxed to this worktree and couldn't list `/tmp/pgraph-run` or the golden tree, so I couldn't run it myself. If you point me at the judged pair's capture directory (or lift the sandbox), that's a two-minute close on this issue either way. I didn't request `vk/blit.c` — on this evidence an edit there would target a defect that isn't in it.
